$comment: Pinned disclosed upstream state for SEC-2 and SEC-7.
This file is NOT an exclude list and NOT a threshold reduction. Each gate below
still runs in full; the rubric asserts that the finding set it produces is
EXACTLY this set. A new finding, a changed finding, or a disappeared finding all
FAIL the gate and force a human back to this file. Emptying an entry is the only
way a finding leaves the rubric, and that requires the upstream fix to have
landed.
Rationale for pinning rather than letting the gate stand red: a permanently-red
gate reports the same colour whether or not a NEW vulnerability appeared, so it
detects nothing. An exact-set assertion keeps detection alive while representing
the known, unfixed, upstream-owned state honestly and visibly in every report.
The audit covers the whole installed graph, not `--prod`. Dev dependencies are
not outside the boundary: they execute in CI with the checkout and the runner's
environment in reach, and they resolve from the same lockfile as the shipped
build. A dev-only advisory is disclosed here as its own entry with its own owner
and sunset, never excluded by scope. The full-graph audit currently reports NO
advisory at or above the gated severity, which is why the list below is empty.
GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p (ws, high) was disclosed here and is RETIRED at the
greater-v0.13.0 pin bump. The entry's own sunset named this exact condition:
"Delete this entry at the first `greater` CLI pin bump whose adapters release
resolves ws >= 8.21.0." greater-v0.13.0 bumped graphql-ws to 6.2.0, which
resolves ws@8.21.0, so the vulnerable range >=8.0.0 <8.21.0 no longer contains
the installed version. `pnpm audit` reports zero advisories across the WHOLE
graph, not only --prod.
The entry is deleted rather than kept with a note, because SEC-2 asserts the
finding set is EXACTLY this list: a retired advisory left in place fails the
gate just as loudly as a new one appearing, and that symmetry is the whole
design. An empty list is not a weakened gate — a new advisory now fails SEC-2
immediately, which is the strongest this check has been.

must_pass_reason: These are the two integrity properties the gate exists for: every vendored
component file the manifest records is present, and nothing extra is sitting
under the vendored root. They are non-negotiable and are asserted PASS.
SEC-7 fails if either regresses, regardless of anything disclosed below.

disclosed_failures.name: NPM Dependencies
summary: The blog face's registry manifest requires the shared `content` module,
which carries MarkdownRenderer.svelte and CodeBlock.svelte and pulls a full
Markdown rendering chain. The face's own Article.Content deliberately
refuses to render Markdown — lesser owns canonical rendering — so the
renderer arrives through a sibling module the reading surface never uses.
Contentus declines to install that chain: installing it to satisfy a
checker would ship a second canonical renderer and break the renderer-
authority invariant this repo exists to hold. See
docs/consumption/renderer-authority.md.
sunset: Delete this entry the day the blog face stops requiring the `content`
shared module, or the day the Markdown chain moves out of it. The same day
$comment: VERSION RANGES MOVED AT THE greater-v0.13.0 PIN BUMP, and the finding did not.
The same thirteen dependencies are still required by the blog face's registry
manifest and still declined here; three of them are simply required at newer
ranges by the v0.13.0 registry (@apollo/client ^4.0.9 -> 4.2.9,
@apollo/client-react-streaming ^0.14.0 -> ^0.14.5, viem ^2.47.14 -> ^2.55.10).
SEC-7 asserts the disclosed set EXACTLY, so a moved range reads as one finding
retired and another appearing — which is the gate working. The strings are
updated to what `greater doctor` now reports; nothing was installed and the
reason for declining is unchanged.
graphql@^16.12.0 LEFT THIS LIST AT M2, and it left it by being installed rather
than by being re-declined. Contentus now validates every GraphQL document it can
send against lesser's pinned canonical schema (scripts/audit-graphql-contract.mjs),
and that validation uses graphql-js — the reference parser and validator — as a
DEVDEPENDENCY at build time. It is not the Apollo runtime client and not part of
the declined Markdown chain: nothing in src/ imports it, the tiny same-origin
transport in src/lib/cms/graphql.ts is unchanged, and the twelve dependencies still
listed above are still declined for the reasons stated.
The version is greater's floor, not the newest release. graphql 17.0.2 installed
cleanly and every API this repository uses is identical in both, but it raised a
fresh `greater doctor` warning — "Manifest vs Required Floors": graphql 17.0.2 vs
required ^16.12.0 — and the honest answer to a floor a peer declares is to meet it,
not to disclose past it. Adding a disclosure where a one-line fix exists is how a
pin becomes a place to put problems.

summary: components.json declares the CLI's default alias set. Contentus vendors
only the faces and shared modules it consumes, so src/lib/components/ui and
src/lib/primitives are never created. Creating empty directories to silence
a checker would be exactly the cosmetic workaround this rubric refuses.
These are pinned so that a THIRD warning — which would mean a real alias
regression — fails SEC-7.
`Alias Path: utils` WAS pinned here and is now retired, which is what this
list is supposed to do. M4 vendored the social face's shared modules, whose
registry manifest places notificationGrouping.ts at `lib/utils/`; the `utils`
alias target src/lib/utils therefore exists and the check passes on its own.
It was removed rather than left in place because SEC-7 fails a disclosed
finding that has started passing — the retirement path working as designed,
not a silencing.
